how_to_edit: Visitors of merit: named people who call at the Hearth on a schedule, give quests, and (for traders) open a shop that grows as you earn their favour. Read by scripts/game/visitor_service.gd.

schedule: first_day = the first day they can turn up; every_days = how often they come back; stay_days = how many days they stay each visit. requires (optional): {"clear": dungeon_id} or {"flag": story_flag} before they ever come.
ranks: favour needed for each rank, lowest first. Favour comes from quest rewards and mini-game wins.
art: portrait/sprite paths. Leave them empty and the game draws a dark silhouette with a question mark (art still to come).

quest objective types: kills {family, count} (families: sporeling, bandit, undead) · reach_floor {dungeon, floor} · clear {dungeon, class?, max_seconds?, max_potions?} · return_gold {gold} (come home alive carrying at least this much) · runs_home {count} (adventurers coming home alive) · train {count} (training sessions) · contest_win {count} (beat them at their mini-game) · deliver {food: id, count} or {gold: amount} (handed over in person).
quest fields: requires_rank (index into ranks), requires_quests (ids that must be finished first), lines.offer / lines.progress / lines.done (what they say).
reward fields: gold, renown, favour, items (armory item ids), furnishings (lodging furnishing ids), food {id: count}, flag (a story flag other content can check).
shop: offers sold once the visitor's rank reaches min_rank. kind: item (armory id), furnishing (lodging id), food (pantry id, count). price in gold. once: true = sold a single time.
minigame: one of arm_wrestling, memory_match, quick_draw, drinking, with the visitor's stat score; a win gives favour_per_win, once per visit.

mayor_corvin_rook.name: Corvin Rook
mayor_corvin_rook.title: Mayor of the Crossroads
mayor_corvin_rook.art_brief: Late fifties, ink-stained cuffs, a chain of office he keeps tucking under his coat. Tired, decent, always counting something.
mayor_corvin_rook.blurb: The town's mayor. He doesn't care which god gets the credit, only whether the roads stay open and people eat.

greeting: Keeper. Corvin Rook, mayor, for my sins. The town's watching what you do with this place.
Keeper. The farmers on the east road asked after your people. That's new.
Ah, Keeper. Sit, if you've a moment. The council argued about you for an hour. In a good way.
Keeper. I'll say it plainly: this town would be worse off without the Hearth.
idle: Refugees on the north road again. Nordians, mostly. They say the border holds are emptying.
Every nation wants this crossroads. None of them want to feed it.
Debts, roads, roofs. That's what a town is. The gods can argue about the rest.

quests.title: Open the Briarway
quests.summary: Reach the third floor of the Verdant Forest.

lines.offer: The Briarway's the shortest road east, and nothing's come back up it for a month. Send someone deep enough to tell me what's down there.
lines.progress: No word from the third floor yet. The carters are waiting on you.
lines.done: Three floors down and back to tell it. I'll have the carters try the road. Here, the council's thanks, in coin.

quests.title: Bread for the North Road
quests.summary: Give the mayor 4 Hearty Fare for the refugee camp.

lines.offer: There are families camped by the north bridge. I can't ask the town for more. Could the Hearth spare some proper food? Four rations would see them through the week.
lines.progress: Four rations of Hearty Fare, when you can spare them. No scraps, mind. They've had enough of those.
lines.done: They'll remember who fed them. So will I.

lines.offer: Whatever holds the forest isn't just beasts. The old foresters talk about a heart in the wood that doesn't die. Kill it, Keeper, and the east road is ours again.
lines.progress: The forest still holds. I won't pretend that isn't costing us.
lines.done: The Heartwood's quiet. The council voted you a purse, and for once nobody argued.

quests.title: Under the Ossuary
quests.summary: Reach the Stone Crypt beneath the forest.

lines.offer: The foresters say there's stone under the roots. Old stone, older than the town. I need to know if it's a cellar or a grave.
lines.progress: Nothing from below the forest yet.
lines.done: A crypt. Under my town. Keep this quiet, Keeper. If the nations hear there's a prison at the crossroads, they'll come with more than refugees.

tessaly_vane.name: Tessaly Vane
tessaly_vane.title: Nordian Arms-Trader
tessaly_vane.art_brief: Broad-shouldered, forties, a fur-lined travelling coat over a smith's apron. A border-hold oath ring on her left hand. Laughs loudly, haggles harder.
tessaly_vane.blurb: A travelling smith from the Nordian border holds. She sells only to people she's seen prove themselves.

greeting: Hm. A tavern keeper buying swords? Show me your people can use them first.
Back again. Your kobold-killers have been talked about on the road.
Keeper! Come, I've kept the good steel under the cloth for you.
Friend. In the holds we'd call you oath-kin. Take whatever you need.
idle: Steel from the holds, carried four hundred miles. Don't ask for a discount.
The holds want Balor's road closed for good. They'd burn the whole prison to do it.
My brother went south to fight. I went south to sell to the people fighting. One of us is smarter.

lines.offer: Kobolds took two of my mules on the forest road. Kill fifteen of the thieving things and I'll believe your people can hold a blade.
lines.progress: Still counting kobolds. I want fifteen.
lines.done: Fifteen! Ha. My mules are avenged. Here, and come see what's under the cloth.

quests.title: A Proven Blade
quests.summary: Defeat the forest's guardian with a Warrior.

lines.offer: In the holds a blade isn't proven until it's held a line. Send a warrior through the forest to its guardian and back, and I'll give them a shield worth the name.
lines.progress: A warrior, through the whole forest. No mages hiding behind them.
lines.done: That's a held line. The shield's yours. Sentinel steel, hold-forged.

lines.offer: Old crypt-bone makes the best quench there is. Don't look at me like that. Put down twenty-five of the dead below the forest and I'll make it worth your while.
lines.progress: Twenty-five of the dead. I've got the forge ready.
lines.done: Good bone. The holds would call this grave-robbing. The holds can buy their swords elsewhere.

calden_ashwick.name: Calden Ashwick
calden_ashwick.title: Helvetican Physician
calden_ashwick.art_brief: Thin, thirties, spectacles, a physician's satchel crusted with road dust. Licensed by a civic league he no longer quite believes in.
calden_ashwick.blurb: A league physician travelling the border towns. He believes rest and food save more lives than any blessing.

greeting: Good day. Calden Ashwick, physician. Your people look underfed. That's an observation, not an insult.
Keeper. Your adventurers are sleeping better. I can tell from the colour of them.
Ah, the Keeper. I've written to the league about the Hearth. They didn't reply. They rarely do.
Keeper. If the leagues ran their infirmaries like you run this place, I'd still be working for them.
idle: The leagues treat the seals like aqueducts: infrastructure to be maintained. I'm not sure the prisoners agree.
Most wounds I see aren't from monsters. They're from hunger and bad sleep.
Spores from the forest get into the lungs. Your people should cover their faces.

lines.offer: The forest spores are spreading into the farms. I need samples, which means someone has to kill the things carrying them. Twenty should do.
lines.progress: Twenty sporelings. Burst them from a distance if you can.
lines.done: Excellent samples. Disgusting, but excellent. Take some proper food for your people; I insist.

quests.title: A Disciplined House
quests.summary: Hold 6 training sessions at the Hearth.

lines.offer: Training is medicine too, done properly. Six sessions, Keeper. Show me the Hearth takes its people seriously.
lines.progress: Keep them training. Steady, not cruel.
lines.done: Six sessions and nobody broken. Here: an herb garden for one of the rooms. Good for the lungs.

quests.title: Bring Them Home
quests.summary: Have 3 adventurers come home alive from their expeditions.

lines.offer: Every tavern on this road sends people into the dark. Very few send them home. Do it three times and I'll stop worrying about you.
lines.progress: Three adventurers, home and breathing. Retreating counts. Dying doesn't.
lines.done: Three home. That's rarer than you'd think, Keeper. Much rarer.

grey_archivist.name: The Grey Archivist
grey_archivist.title: Seeker from the Veiled Isles
grey_archivist.art_brief: Hooded, age hard to tell, grey travelling robes stitched with tide charts. Carries a sealed book they never open in company. Never seen eating.
grey_archivist.blurb: A quiet investigator from the Isles who keeps accounts of things other empires renamed. Appears only after the forest's guardian falls.

greeting: You killed the heart of the wood. Did you ask what it was guarding?
Keeper. You've started asking questions. Good.
Keeper. My book has a page for this tavern now. That has not happened in a long time.
Keeper. When the Hearth forgets, I will remember for you. That is a promise.
idle: The gods did not build the prisons alone. Ask who held the other end of the chain.
This building is older than your town. You know that, don't you?
Every prisoner has a name the victors stopped using.

quests.title: Below the Roots
quests.summary: Reach the third floor of the Stone Crypt.

lines.offer: The crypt below the forest has carvings on its third floor. I need someone to see them and come back. Remember what you see.
lines.progress: The third floor of the crypt. The carvings are on the walls near the stairs.
lines.done: Chains, and hands on both ends of them. As I feared. Thank you, Keeper.

quests.title: A Heavy Purse
quests.summary: Have an adventurer come home carrying 300 gold or more.

lines.offer: Gold is memory, of a kind: it remembers every hand that held it. Bring me a purse of three hundred from below and I'll read it.
lines.progress: Three hundred, carried home in one trip.
lines.done: This coin was minted before your town existed. Interesting. Keep most of it; I only needed to see.

lines.offer: The thing at the bottom of the crypt wears a crown. Prisoners don't wear crowns, Keeper. Wardens do. Put it down and we'll learn which it was.
lines.progress: The crowned one still sits below.
lines.done: A warden, then, who forgot which side of the door they were on. Write that down somewhere the Hearth can't lose it.
